findings.title: RPI escalator never applied — billed flat since 2021
findings.summary: The agreement indexes the annual fee at each anniversary, but it has been billed flat at $480,000 since 2021. The correct current run-rate is $662,159 — 5 anniversaries of uplift were never billed.
findings.leverage: The Price Adjustment clause entitles Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. to index the fee to RPI (UK, series CHAW, Jan 1987 = 100); the rate has not moved since 2021, so the entitlement is unambiguous. Audit rights cover the last 24 months.
findings.recommendedAsk: Reprice forward to $662,159/yr (+$182,159) and recover the in-window arrears ($438,778 total to date; audit right covers the last 24 months).

findings.title: Introductory 15% discount still applied 9 months past expiry (2025-09-30)
findings.summary: The 15% introductory discount expired 2025-09-30 but billing has continued to apply a discount line on every invoice since — 9 post-expiry months totalling $40,500 of credit that was no longer contractually owed. The list price should have been restored at expiry.
findings.leverage: The Introductory Discount clause is expressly time-boxed to 2025-09-30; every discount credited after that date is recoverable and the list price applies forward. The issue is recent and discrete (9 months), so waiver/estoppel risk is minimal.
findings.recommendedAsk: Restore the list price forward (+$54,000/yr) and recover the $40,500 of discount credited across 9 months after the 2025-09-30 expiry.

findings.title: Take-or-pay minimum shortfall never invoiced — $90,000 under the $600,000 annual floor
findings.summary: The agreement carries an annual take-or-pay minimum of $600,000, but only $510,000 was billed over the trailing 12 months. The $90,000 shortfall is owed under the minimum-commitment clause and was never invoiced.
findings.leverage: The Minimum Commitment (take-or-pay) clause obligates the customer to pay at least $600,000 per measurement year regardless of usage; the entitlement is unconditional. Audit rights cover the last 24 months — the entire shortfall is in-window.
findings.recommendedAsk: Issue a true-up invoice for the $90,000 take-or-pay shortfall under the Minimum Commitment clause (audit right covers the last 24 months; the full gap is in-window).

findings.title: Fuel surcharge (8.5%) never billed
findings.summary: The agreement entitles Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. to a 8.5% fuel surcharge (EIA on-highway diesel, monthly) on the base recurring fee, but no surcharge line appears on any billing. At the current base run-rate that is $3,740/mo — $44,880 unbilled to date and $44,880/yr going forward.
findings.leverage: The Fuel surcharge clause is an explicit pass-through (EIA on-highway diesel, monthly); the surcharge is a fixed 8.5% of the base fee, so the entitlement is mechanical and unambiguous. Audit rights cover the last 24 months.
findings.recommendedAsk: Add the Fuel surcharge line (8.5% of base = $3,740/mo) to billing going forward (+$44,880/yr) and back-bill the in-window arrears ($44,880 to date; audit right covers the last 24 months).

findings.ruleName: Auto-renewal repriced at the old rate
findings.title: Evergreen renewal billed at the old rate — list rose to $58,000/mo on 2025-09-01, still billing $54,000/mo
findings.summary: The agreement auto-renewed on 2025-09-01 and the rate card's effective list price stepped up from $54,000 to $58,000/mo, but billing has continued at the pre-renewal $54,000/mo for 10 months. The recurring rate was never repriced to the renewal list.
findings.leverage: The renewal carried the current rate card forward at $58,000/mo (effective 2025-09-01); billing kept the lapsed $54,000 rate. The gap is recent (10 months), well inside the 24-month audit window, so the correction is clean.
findings.recommendedAsk: Reprice forward to the renewal list of $58,000/mo (+$48,000/yr) and recover the 10 months billed at the lapsed rate ($40,000 to date; well within the 24-month audit window).

findings.title: Scheduled price step (2025-10-01) never applied — still billing $52,000/mo
findings.summary: The pricing schedule raised the monthly recurring fee to $56,000 effective 2025-10-01, but the last 9 billings still charge $52,000/mo — a $4,000/mo shortfall. Correct the rate forward and back-bill the in-window arrears.
findings.leverage: The Scheduled Price Increase clause fixes a dated, agreed step to $56,000.00/mo effective 2025-10-01; the entitlement is explicit and every under-billed month sits inside the 24-month audit window.
findings.recommendedAsk: Reprice forward to $56,000/mo (+$48,000/yr) and recover the $36,000 of arrears billed below the stepped rate since 2025-10-01.
findings.clauseCited: Scheduled Price Increase (Schedule B, Year-3 step)

findings.title: Graduated tier breached — premium-capacity rate never billed above 4,000 units
findings.summary: Volume runs at 5,200 units/mo, but billing applies the base rate of $12 flat across the whole quantity. The 1,200 units above the 4,000-unit break should price at $15. Correct graduated charge is $66,000/mo vs. $62,400 billed — under by $3,600/mo across 11 completed months.
findings.leverage: The graduated tier schedule entitles Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. to bill $15 on volume above 4,000 units. The breach is recent and the over-tier volume is on the invoices, so the entitlement is unambiguous and well inside the 24-month audit window.
findings.recommendedAsk: Re-rate forward to the graduated schedule ($66,000/mo, +$43,200/yr) and recover the in-window arrears of $39,600 across the last 11 months under the Volume Tier Pricing clause.

findings.title: Overage above the 8,000-unit allowance never billed — 1,500 units/mo unbilled
findings.summary: Metered usage averages 9,500 units/mo against a bundled allowance of 8,000 units, but no overage line was raised. The contracted overage rate of $2/unit applies to the 1,500-unit monthly excess — $3,000/mo ($36,000/yr) that has gone unbilled across 12 months.
findings.leverage: The Overage / Excess-Usage clause entitles Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. to bill consumption above the 8,000-unit allowance at $2/unit. Metered usage is the seller's own record, so the excess is unambiguous; audit rights cover the last 24 months.
findings.recommendedAsk: Raise the unbilled overage ($36,000 to date across 12 months) and bill the overage line going forward at $3,000/mo (+$36,000/yr).

findings.ruleName: Credits issued in excess of contracted rate
findings.title: Rebate over-applied — 8.0% credited vs 5.0% contracted
findings.summary: The agreement grants a valid 5.0% volume rebate (effective through 2027-12-31), but billing applied credits averaging 8.0% of gross — over-crediting by 3.0% across 12 month(s). Excess credit given to date is $18,000; left uncorrected the forward leak is $18,000/yr.
findings.leverage: The Volume Rebate clause fixes the discount at 5.0% of gross; credits beyond that are unsupported and recoverable. The rebate is still in force (expires 2027-12-31), so this is an over-application — not a lapsed-discount dispute. Audit rights cover the last 24 months.
findings.recommendedAsk: Correct the rebate line to the contracted 5.0% (stops the $18,000/yr forward leak) and recover the $18,000 over-credited to date under the audit/true-up clause.

findings.title: 6 delivered work orders never billed — $15,000 unrecognized
findings.summary: 6 special-handling / expedited jobs were delivered and accepted but never invoiced — no billing line references their work-order numbers. At the contracted unit price these total $15,000 of completed, unbilled service revenue.
findings.leverage: The work orders are signed-off as delivered at the contracted unit price; the entitlement is unambiguous and the entire amount sits within the 24-month audit window. Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. can issue corrected invoices immediately.
findings.recommendedAsk: Issue corrected invoices for the 6 delivered work orders ($15,000 total). The amount is fully in-window and supported by signed delivery records.
findings.clauseCited: Services & Fees (billing for delivered work orders)

findings.title: Late-payment interest (1.5%/mo) never charged on 2 past-due invoices
findings.summary: The agreement entitles Northwind Logistics Group, Inc. to a 1.5%/mo finance charge on balances past due, but no interest has been billed. $130,000 sits past due beyond the 30-day grace period; the accrued unbilled interest to date is $5,400.
findings.leverage: The Late Payment / finance-charge clause sets a 1.5%/mo rate on past-due balances; the entitlement is mechanical once an invoice ages past the grace period. The exposure is recent (oldest item 130 days past due), so it sits squarely inside the 24-month audit window.
findings.recommendedAsk: Issue a finance-charge invoice for $5,400 in accrued late-payment interest under the Late Payment clause (1.5%/mo on balances past the 30-day grace period).
